      "title": "Adding FromContext to Logger interface breaks all implementations not updated",
      "body": "The Logger interface gains a new method, FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. This is a breaking change for any type implementing this interface. The PR updates only grafanaInfraLogWrapper and TestLogger. If the repository contains other implementations (e.g., additional test fakes or alternative loggers), they will fail to compile. All implementations must be updated, or a default adapter should be provided."
    },

      "file": "pkg/plugins/log/logger.go",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "FromContext type assertion can silently drop contextual attributes",
      "body": "The method asserts that d.l.FromContext(ctx) returns a *log.ConcreteLogger. If the underlying FromContext returns a different concrete type (e.g., a wrapper or decorated logger), the assertion fails and the code falls back to d.New(), which discards all context attributes. Consequently, log entries produced by LoggerMiddleware that rely on FromContext may lose pluginId, endpoint, dsName, etc. A more robust approach should preserve attributes even if the returned logger type differs."
    },

      "body": "The newly added ContextualLoggerMiddleware is responsible for enriching the request context with plugin and request details for several endpoints. There are no tests verifying that the context passed to the next middleware contains the expected attributes, or that the middleware correctly passes through unchanged for stream endpoints. This leaves a significant behavior change untested."
    },

    },

      "line": 161,

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger interface breaks all implementations not updated
findings.body: The Logger interface gains a new method, FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. This is a breaking change for any type implementing this interface. The PR updates only grafanaInfraLogWrapper and TestLogger. If the repository contains other implementations (e.g., additional test fakes or alternative loggers), they will fail to compile. All implementations must be updated, or a default adapter should be provided.

findings.title: FromContext type assertion can silently drop contextual attributes
findings.body: The method asserts that d.l.FromContext(ctx) returns a *log.ConcreteLogger. If the underlying FromContext returns a different concrete type (e.g., a wrapper or decorated logger), the assertion fails and the code falls back to d.New(), which discards all context attributes. Consequently, log entries produced by LoggerMiddleware that rely on FromContext may lose pluginId, endpoint, dsName, etc. A more robust approach should preserve attributes even if the returned logger type differs.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no unit tests
findings.body: The newly added ContextualLoggerMiddleware is responsible for enriching the request context with plugin and request details for several endpoints. There are no tests verifying that the context passed to the next middleware contains the expected attributes, or that the middleware correctly passes through unchanged for stream endpoints. This leaves a significant behavior change untested.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware change to use FromContext is not covered by tests
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now uses m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) instead of directly logging with m.logger and manually appended fields such as pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName, and dsUID. No tests were updated or added to verify that these fields are still present when the ContextualLoggerMiddleware is in the chain, nor that logging still works when the middleware is used without the contextual logger.

findings.title: Logger name still says 'plugin.instrumentation' after rename
findings.body: The logger passed to NewLoggerMiddleware is still created with log.New("plugin.instrumentation"). Since the PR renames instrumentation to metrics and separates contextual logging, this logger name is now misleading. Consider renaming it to something like "plugin.logger" or "plugin.request" to reflect its actual purpose.

findings.title: Test function name not updated after middleware rename
findings.body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware, while the middleware type and constructor have been renamed to MetricsMiddleware. Renaming the test function to TestMetricsMiddleware would improve consistency and avoid confusion.
